chapter: Childhood, family and the sounds of New Orleans
title: Contraband seafood peddlers and the police
summary: Black fish peddlers on fast wagons dodged police who confiscated their catch on Fridays.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Now, every peddler... You had charcoal peddlers, you had vegetable peddlers, you had the milk peddlers. Then you had the contraband fish and shrimp and seafood peddler, who generally had a fast horse and a light wagon, who could run. Because you weren't allowed to sell seafood out in the public. It had to be under supervision because of the spoilage. But these guys would come along on Friday, which was the fast day. They had seafood; they had no meat. They had a wagon, and inside this wagon they'd have, they'd have shrimps, they'd have a vast variety of fish, a couple of turtles -- (?) more than one. But they were always on the move, looking out for the cops. Because the cops would generally try to catch them, to confiscate all the fish, bring them to jail, bring them out to the Fifth Precinct (in this neighborhood, in my particular neighborhood), and when they'd get there, they'd take all the provisions and split them up amongst the Police Department. The old folks said, "Oh, the police got the poor man. All that good fish, all

them policemen's goin' to take all that fish and bring it home." Whatever he had, man. They didn't have no refrigeration in jail, so they'd keep in jail overnight. Because it's against the law, the sanitation law. And generally, he had to get somebody to speak for him...

It was a racket. You'd lose your day's provisions, and they might send you home. So the Negroes generally had fast horses. See, the police had horses, too, you know. So if you was on foot, you had a chance. But generally, when automobiles came along, them little Fords just pulled right up, right in front of the horses, they'd stop and go to jail. "What you got in there?" They'd look under the cart, because sometimes he'd keep some shrimps under there.
